title: The Release Gate
kicker: Nothing goes live until it passes every check
tagline: Tests, then a practice run. Anything that isn't all green waits.
what: Before a release can go live, every test runs against a throwaway copy of real data. Then a program clicks through the practice site the way a person would, and it has to come back green.
built: Each test run gets its own fresh copy of the data, thrown away after
A release goes live only once every test passes on the exact code going out
A program has to click through the practice site and come back green before anything goes live
If a check doesn't finish, the release waits for the next run instead of going out
starring: Every release, before anyone at work sees it

making.problem: A change could pass its own tests and still break the real site, because the tests never saw real data or clicked through real pages.

moment.what: Now every release proves itself the way a person would, on real pages, before anyone else sees it. If it isn't green, it waits.

frames.name: Test on a copy
frames.says: Every test runs against a fresh, throwaway copy of the real data.

frames.name: Click through it
frames.says: Then a program clicks through a practice copy of the site, the way a person would.

frames.name: Green or it waits
frames.says: Only an all-green release goes live. Anything else waits for the next run.
